correctness.rationale: The six permutations of increments {1,2,4} translated over Z15 yield exactly 90 distinct tetrahedra, f-vector (15,105,180,90), and complete graph edges. Freudenthal triangulation of R³ has deck quotient by ker(a+2b+4c mod15), so H1(K,Z)≅ker(phi)≅Z³, not merely a finite modular-rank inference. The seven representative edge lift vectors for differences 1..7 and their negatives for 8..14 vanish on all actual 180 faces. An independently written exhaustive vertex-triple census counted 455−180=275 missing triangles; every boundary maps to nonzero primitive lattice displacement. Exactly seven sign classes occur with multiplicities 45 each six times, and one multiplicity 5, whose missing triangles are {i,i+5,i+10}. Inspected verifier constructs full order-120 automorphism group from published generators and explicitly exhausts the five systolic cycle orbits and class action. No simple cycle can have fewer than three edges.

originality.rationale: The exact 15-vertex T³, its universal-cover lattice/neighborliness, facet list, and symmetry group were published by Kühnel–Lassmann and tabulated by Köhler–Lutz (2005 table p29). The accessible full-text 2005 paper lists f-vector (105,180,90), T³, group 5:4×S3 and facet orbits, not the 275 integral primitive triangle homology-class distribution. The highly relevant 1984 Kühnel–Lassmann original could not be fully inspected; authorized Oxford retrieval was safety-blocked after OA search failed, and no override was attempted. Therefore full-paper noncoverage for 1984 is not claimed and unindexed prior explicit computations remain residual risks. Current statement-level evidence supports best-of-knowledge originality without asserting certainty.
